acceptance.expected: Execution token verifier rejects 9 cases; valid token accepted; 4 s skew accepted
acceptance.actual: Rejected with a distinct asserted reason: foreign signature (+ tampered payload), unknown kid, iss != gxg-executor, aud != own ID (+ aud as list), exp > 5 s past, iat > 5 s future, each of 13 required claims missing, alg none / HS256, jti replay. Also typ, lifetime > 60 s, malformed. Valid accepted; exp 4 s past and iat 4 s future accepted. JWKS cache: <= 10 min, removed kid rejected after refresh, failed refresh trusts no key (AS-09, AS-10). Cycle 2: AS-11 boundary exp = now − 5 and iat = now + 5 accepted; accepted token replayed at T0 + 30 and at exp + 5 → replay; oversized signed token → malformed; X25519 JWK ignored; ExecutorJwks.readiness() (MCC-09). Cycle 3: claims validated by execution-token.schema.json (sub/jti must be UUIDs, ahs/tool/idk bounds, no extra claims → 'claims'); jti of wrong type → claim:jti; JWKS outage: one fetch per 5 s back-off, not per call or /readyz (fetch counter)

acceptance.expected: Bundle with built_at older than 24 h -> not ready (GR-13)

interpretations_for_owner: Service JWT kid: resolved by the spec (AS-06a: kid = RFC 7638 thumbprint; AS-06: 1-2 public_keys, any accepted). Implemented as specified; pinned by the RFC 8037 §A.3 vector.
Service JWT 'wrong iss' case: the receiving endpoint passes its issuer allowlist (AS-06 'service -> endpoint'); outside it -> rejected. 'iss not in registry' is a separate rejection.
GR-13 staleness is measured by built_at (AC-M1-07); resolved by GR-13a (CI re-signs at least every 12 h).
Groups: the resolver expands group:<id> itself, so both GR-11a (expanded) and raw files work; an unknown group grants nobody.
Reload: a failed load keeps the previous valid bundle; anti-rollback is now GR-13a (older than the loaded or the on-disk max built_at, or later than now + 5 s → rejected), implemented as specified.
known_limitations: The M2 builder is not available yet: compatibility with GR-11a is tested only against an in-test builder (canonical.dumps + Ed25519 over the exact bytes). The loader does not require the bytes to be JCS-canonical; it only verifies the signature over them.
Base64url decoding accepts non-zero trailing bits (needed: the synthetic keys in registry.example.yaml, e.g. 'BBBB…', are non-canonical but match the schema).
JWKS transport is injected (fetch()); no HTTP client. Execution token issuance, EFF-18 п.2–5, Approval Service client and MCP tool-error wrapper are left to M3/M7/M8.
IdentityVerifier has only the test-profile stub (GXG_PROFILE=test); the real mechanism waits for the M4 spike. Stub assertions carry no body hash.
jti caches are in-memory per process; EFF-20 relies on dispatch CAS as the real one-time guard.
Two conftest.py files clash in a single mypy run; the root conftest.py is type-checked in a separate mypy --strict step.

jsonschema checks `format: date-time` only when rfc3339-validator is installed (it is in the dev env, not a kit dependency); without it the loader's own parser still rejects malformed or zone-less timestamps (test_expiry_without_time_zone_is_rejected_without_a_format_checker).
Schema copies in src/gxg_connector_kit/schemas/ must be refreshed when schemas/ changes; tests/test_schema.py fails until they are (a symlink breaks uv build: 'Is a directory').

survivors.reason: `not isinstance(kid, str) or not kid` → `and`: PyJWT already rejects a non-string kid as malformed; an empty kid then reaches key_for, matches no JWKS kid / no thumbprint → the same 'kid' rejection
PyJWT option key `verify_nbf` renamed: PyJWT then uses its default (check nbf only if present); neither token type has nbf, so tokens of our issuers are judged the same
PyJWT option key `verify_iss` renamed: default verify_iss is True, but we pass no `issuer`, and PyJWT skips the check when issuer is None; iss is checked by our allowlist
`_keys = None`: never read before the first _current() assigns it (_refetch_at = -inf forces a fetch on first use)
`float("-INF")`: Python parses it case-insensitively, same value
`cast(None, claims)`: typing.cast is a no-op at runtime
